messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGE — geo-dns checks failing for eu-west-1; alert threshold breached (5m error rate). auto-pager sent to @maria and @lee :rotating_light:

maria: taking the page, jumping in now. seeing increased SERVFAILs from Cloudflare resolvers to our Route53 authoritative in eu-west-1.

lee: I can confirm tcp/tls handshake timeouts between CF edge resolvers and our ns1 in the eu-west-1 AZ. digging traceroutes.

sam: tagging in network to rule out upstream peering issues. CF status shows no broad outage but their peering logs show repeated TLS renegotiation on some peers.

oncall-bot: Pager duty note: please ack and update channel when mitigations start.

maria: quick customer impact note: synthetic checks show ~12% of read requests to hosted API returning transient DNS errors (mostly SERVFAIL) for eu-west region; global traffic unaffected. will notify CS if impact grows.

lee: running diagnostics:```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 example.redwood.com A +tcp
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; Query time: 230 ms, SERVER: 1.1.1.1#53(1.1.1.1)
```

lee: traceroute from CF resolver to ns1.eu-west-1.internal -> path completes but TLS client hello times out intermittently. looks like session resumption handshake failing.

oz: possible recent cert rotation on our side? Ops pushed k8s secret for ns certs yesterday — checking.

maria: confirm — we rotated zone transfer certs yesterday as part of automation. rolling back to prior cert on ns1 would be disruptive, prefer to test config first.

sam: opening ticket with Cloudflare: "TLS handshake failures to customer authoritative nameservers (SNI mismatch / aborted handshake)" sending logs + pcap to support.

netops-bot: Noted: BGP and peering stable; no packet loss >1%.

lee: quick mitigation option: update geo-dns routing policy to temporarily de-prioritize eu-west-1 authoritative endpoints for CF resolver IP ranges, let Route53 answers come from eu-central or fallback POPs. Can do a weight shift.

maria: do it. we need to be careful about TTLs. set low TTL for the change so rollback is quick.

deploy-bot: geo-dns weight change plan ready: apply change to policy 'geo-eu' to shift 60% traffic off eu-west-1 for CF ASN list. awaiting approval.

maria: approved. deploy-bot, apply now and set ttl=60s. annotate change: "mitigate CF->ns TLS handshake failures — emergency weight shift"

deploy-bot: change applied. propagation started.

lee: running dig again:```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 example.redwood.com +short
93.184.216.34
```

lee: immediate improvement for CF resolver IPs where we shifted weight. overall SERVFAIL rate down to ~3% in synthetic checks.

maria: contacting top-affected customers with initial note: "We detected intermittent DNS errors affecting eu-west-1; we implemented temporary traffic shift to fallback endpoints to restore service. Engineering investigating root cause."

sam: CF support responded: they saw handshake aborts due to SNI mismatch with our new cert on ns1 — they suggested we ensure SNI matches expected hostname or resume old cert. They also confirmed some of their edge POPs keep old session caches longer which caused repeated failure bursts.

oz: plan: revert to previous cert on ns1 for now and schedule a controlled cert rotation with matching SNI config. I'll prepare the rollback runbook.

maria: rollback steps look safe, low blast radius. do it during mitigation window — coord with deploy-bot for canary then full.

deploy-bot: rolling back ns1 cert on eu-west-1 (canary -> 25% -> 100%). logging to /var/log/dns-cert-ops.

lee: post-rollback checks: dig/tcp/tls all show stable handshakes from CF resolvers. synthetic SERVFAIL rate back to baseline (<0.5%).

maria: closing immediate impact: customers experiencing errors have been restored via weight shift + cert rollback. keeping channel open for postmortem notes.

sam: CF support will follow up with which POPs were affected and recommend session cache TTL adjustments on their side; logging ticket ref 2026-3918.

maria: post-incident actions so we don't repeat: - add automated SNI verification as part of cert rotation job - make geo-dns emergency weight-shift runbook explicit and scriptable - monitor Cloudflare resolver handshake errors by ASN and POP - schedule a joint troubleshooting call with CF network ops

oz: postmortem owner: @oz. ETA for draft: 48h. I'll include exact timeline and command outputs.

maria: tagging @cust-success to push a brief customer-facing incident summary after postmortem. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident resolved status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident severity set to Sev2.

maria: thanks all, handing back to normal on-call.
